hotspots.title: Summer 2009
hotspots.body: The sixth film was moved from November 2008 to July 2009, giving it a summer release and a longer wait for fans.

hotspots.title: Painted in light
hotspots.body: Cinematographer Bruno Delbonnel gave the film its muted, smoky palette. It became the only film in the series nominated for the Academy Award for cinematography.

hotspots.title: The tallest tower
hotspots.body: The astronomy tower, normally a place for star charts, becomes the stage for the film's defining night under a green-lit storm.

hotspots.title: A collector of people
hotspots.body: Jim Broadbent played the genial potions master who gathers promising students, and holds one memory he would rather nobody saw.

hotspots.title: Notes in the margin
hotspots.body: A second-hand textbook covered in handwritten corrections turns Harry into a potions prodigy, and slowly into someone who uses spells he does not understand.

hotspots.title: A family likeness
hotspots.body: Hero Fiennes-Tiffin, nephew of Ralph Fiennes, played the villain as an eleven-year-old boy in a flashback.

hotspots.title: A lake of the dead
hotspots.body: A lonely cave by the sea, a basin that must be emptied, and pale hands in the water: the film's most frightening sequence takes place far from the school.

hotspots.title: A lighter heart
hotspots.body: For all its darkness, the film is often very funny: love potions, jealousy and teenage awkwardness fill its middle hour.

hotspots.title: Trials in the rain
hotspots.body: The film stages its sport mainly as tryouts and a single match, keeping the focus on character rather than spectacle.

hotspots.title: The mark in the sky
hotspots.body: A sickly glow hangs over the castle at the climax. The staff and students raise their wands in silence afterwards, a farewell the film invents for the screen.

collectibles.name: A tiny vial of liquid luck
A broken locket
collectibles.note: The clasp is engraved, but the inside is empty.
